basics.title: Electric Current & Circuits Explained
basics.focus: Connect charge, current, voltage, power and energy. Follow the units in one worked calculation.
basics.note: Watch the explanation and one relevant example, then return to the teacher’s problem.

emf.title: Cells, EMF, terminal voltage & internal resistance
emf.focus: Understand energy supplied per coulomb, internal heating, and why output voltage can differ from EMF.
emf.note: Relate the video’s symbols to the course: Us or E is EMF; R₀ is internal resistance. Then try the 125 V / 115 V / 4 A example.

signs.title: Sign convention for passive components
signs.focus: Choose voltage polarity and current arrows consistently, and interpret a negative result.
signs.note: Keep the physical node names fixed. Use the lesson’s figures for moving the zero reference.

sources.title: Ideal sources
sources.focus: See what each source fixes: voltage for a voltage source, current for a current source.
sources.note: The connected circuit determines the other quantity. Use the teacher’s examples to check supplied versus absorbed power.

capacitor.title: Capacitor i–v equations
capacitor.focus: Focus on i = C du/dt: capacitor current depends on how fast its voltage changes.
capacitor.note: For Chapter 1, concentrate on the derivative relation, units and marked references. The integral treatment can wait.

inductor.title: Inductor equations
inductor.focus: Focus on u = L di/dt: inductor voltage depends on how fast its current changes.
inductor.note: For Chapter 1, concentrate on the derivative relation, units and marked references. The integral treatment can wait.

transformation.title: Source transformation in network analysis
transformation.focus: Convert a voltage source with series resistance into a current source with parallel resistance, and back.
transformation.note: Keep the same external terminals, resistance and source direction. Return to the teacher’s 5 V / 2 mA network after one example.

topology.title: Loop, Mesh, Node and Branch
topology.focus: Recognise junctions, branches, closed paths and meshes before writing equations.
topology.note: Your teacher counts essential nodes where three or more elements meet and paths between them as branches. Some videos also count ordinary two-element junctions.

kirchhoff.title: Kirchhoff’s Laws and Circuit Analysis
kirchhoff.focus: Write current balance at nodes and signed voltage balance around loops, then solve for branch currents.
kirchhoff.note: Watch the setup and one complete example. Then write the teacher’s five equations for five branch currents, using the assigned arrows.

superposition.title: Superposition Theorem
superposition.focus: Consider independent sources separately and add their signed current or voltage contributions.
superposition.note: Inactive ideal voltage sources become shorts; inactive ideal current sources become opens. Keep resistances. Do not add the separate powers.

thevenin.title: Thévenin’s Theorem Explained
thevenin.focus: Remove the load, find the open-circuit voltage and resistance seen at its port, then reconnect the load.
thevenin.note: Focus on the principle and independent-source example. Dependent-source examples go beyond the current chapter’s worked problems. Then try the teacher’s 8 Ω bridge load.

norton.title: Norton’s Theorem Explained
norton.focus: Find the short-circuit current and parallel equivalent resistance at the same load port.
norton.note: Focus on independent sources. Compare with the Thévenin result: the teacher’s reconnected 8 Ω load must still carry 1 A.

introduction.title: Schematic Diagrams & Symbols
introduction.focus: Recognise the battery, switch, wires and load in a circuit diagram.
introduction.note: Use the sheet below for your teacher’s power-versus-signal and source/link/load classifications.

conditions.title: Open, Closed, and Short Circuits
conditions.focus: Distinguish a conducting load path, a broken path and a direct short.
conditions.note: This is the dedicated lesson 1.3 video. The source-loss and 125 V example are summarised below.

branch-analysis.title: Branch Current Method Explained
branch-analysis.focus: Assign branch currents and use KCL and KVL to form simultaneous equations.
branch-analysis.note: Then apply the same setup to your teacher’s five-branch symbolic example; a negative solution reverses the assumed current direction.

transient-intro.title: Transient Analysis: Behaviour of Basic Circuit Elements
transient-intro.focus: See why a switching event makes R, L and C respond differently.
transient-intro.note: The video explains switching and element behavior. The sheet adds your teacher’s lamp demonstration and applications; its microsecond/millisecond examples are not a universal duration limit.

switching.title: Transient Analysis: Solved Examples on First order RC and RL Circuits
switching.focus: Use capacitor-voltage and inductor-current continuity in worked switching examples.
switching.note: The video revises continuity and solves RC/RL examples. It also previews time constants from 2.3. The examples below use your teacher’s own circuits.

three-values.title: Transient Analysis: First order R C and R L Circuits
three-values.focus: Derive the exponential and find initial value, final value and time constant.
three-values.note: The video derives RC/RL responses and the final + (initial − final) shortcut. The sheet keeps the additional initial-value circuits, final-value examples and unit corrections taught in your course.

rc-response.title: RC Circuits Physics Problems, Time Constant Explained, Capacitor Charging and Discharging
rc-response.focus: Follow charging, discharging and a time-to-target calculation.
rc-response.note: The video explains RC charging, discharging, τ and a threshold calculation. The sheet adds the teacher’s source-to-source complete response and the passive-reference current sign.

rl-response.title: RL Circuits - Inductors & Resistors
rl-response.focus: Calculate RL current buildup, decay and time constants; keep the voltage reference explicit.
rl-response.note: The video covers RL buildup, decay and time constants. It sometimes describes induced EMF or loop traversal drops as negative. Your course’s passive terminal voltage is uL = +L diL/dt; induced EMF is eL = −L diL/dt. Use the marked reference, not the word “voltage” alone.

ac-waveforms.title: Alternating Current vs Direct Current - Rms Voltage, Peak Current & Average Power of AC Circuits
ac-waveforms.focus: Compare AC and DC and calculate peak and RMS values for sinusoids.
ac-waveforms.note: The video covers AC/DC and sine-wave RMS calculations. Its power examples assume sinusoidal in-phase voltage/current; for a general load, use P = UI cosφ in 3.6. The sheet adds your teacher’s frequency and phase material.

phasors.title: Phasor and The Phasor Diagram in AC Circuits Explained
phasors.focus: Connect a rotating vector to a sinusoid and represent magnitude and phase mathematically.
phasors.note: The video teaches rotating vectors, mathematical forms and R/L/C phase relationships. It mainly uses peak phasors. Your course calculations below use RMS phasors; the phase angles are unchanged. The sheet also includes the course’s complex-number arithmetic.

impedance.title: Impedance
impedance.focus: Derive the impedance of R, L and C from their voltage–current laws.
impedance.note: Khan Academy derives each impedance from its element law using complex exponentials. Its cosine/exponential derivation gives the same impedance laws as your course’s sine reference. The sheet states the phase relationships and corrects the capacitor slide labels.

series-rlc.title: Series RLC Circuits, Resonant Frequency, Inductive Reactance & Capacitive Reactance - AC Circuits
series-rlc.focus: Calculate reactances, total impedance magnitude and element voltages in a series circuit.
series-rlc.note: The video calculates a series RLC example, reactances, current and element voltage magnitudes. It calls |Z| “impedance”; your course also requires complex Z and the impedance divider, shown below. Its final resonant-frequency calculation is extra to the reviewed lesson.

parallel-rlc.title: Parallel RLC Circuit Example Problem
parallel-rlc.focus: Calculate parallel branch currents and verify their vector sum.
parallel-rlc.note: The video works a pure parallel RLC example and checks the vector current sum. The sheet adds your teacher’s general complex branches and current-divider examples. The final resonance calculation is optional beyond the reviewed lesson.

average-power.title: Average Power in AC Circuits
average-power.focus: Average instantaneous power over a cycle and distinguish resistive and reactive behavior.
average-power.note: The first video revisits instantaneous power and derives average power; the second introduces apparent power and power factor. The sheet adds your teacher’s signed reactive power, pure-element cases and addition rules. Capacitor sizing is not part of this reviewed lesson. The videos use peak phasors for some derivations and cosine waveforms; use the RMS factors and consistent sine reference stated below.

power-triangle.title: Apparent Power & Power Factor
power-triangle.focus: Relate RMS apparent power to real power and leading or lagging power factor.
power-triangle.note: The first video revisits instantaneous power and derives average power; the second introduces apparent power and power factor. The sheet adds your teacher’s signed reactive power, pure-element cases and addition rules. Capacitor sizing is not part of this reviewed lesson. The videos use peak phasors for some derivations and cosine waveforms; use the RMS factors and consistent sine reference stated below.
